walkthroughs.body_html:
Water is polar — and that changes everything.

Hydrogen bonds between H₂O molecules give:
- High specific heat (4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹) — thermal stability for oceans, blood.
- Cohesion — the xylem column hangs together.
- Solvent — dissolves polar/ionic solutes for transport.

- Carbohydrates — monomer monosaccharide (glucose C₆H₁₂O₆); polymer starch, glycogen, cellulose.
- Lipids — glycerol + fatty acids → triglycerides; phospholipids form membranes.
- Proteins — amino acid monomers join by peptide bonds.
- Nucleic acids — nucleotides join by phosphodiester bonds.

The unifying reaction:

Condensation: 2 monomers → polymer + H₂O.
Hydrolysis: polymer + H₂O → monomers.

n monomers form n-1 bonds, so release n-1 water molecules. Digestion is hydrolysis — amylase splits starch, proteases split proteins.
